title: Omo Kibish Formation (Omo I and Omo II, Ethiopia)
summary: Sediments in the lower Omo Valley of southern Ethiopia that yielded the Omo I and Omo II hominid fossils, among the oldest Homo sapiens remains known. A 2022 study dated the volcanic ash above Omo I to 233,000 years, give or take 22,000, as a minimum age for the fossils.

uncertainty.note: Vidal et al. (2022) give 233 ± 22 kyr (2 sigma) for the KHS Tuff overlying the Omo I member, a minimum age. McDougall et al. (2005) preferred 195 ± 5 kyr. The range lower bound is the 233 kyr minimum with its error; the true age may be older. The start has no upper bound from the opened pages.

as_recorded.value: new minimum age for the Omo fossils of 233 ± 22 kyr
preferred estimate of the age of the Kibish hominids is 195 ± 5 kyr

reviewer_note: Age is a minimum from the overlying tuff and is revised from the 2005 value. Pin is the dated tuff locality at Nakaa-kire near the Omo II site, 5 24.6 N, 35 54.5 E, from the McDougall supplementary table listing; the Wikidata point for the formation (4.80 N, 35.97 E) is about 67 km south and was not used. The Omo I find spot is not given on opened pages, so uncertainty is 10 km. Page text for the Vidal paper opened via PubMed Central.
